To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an expression model of Glut1-Gfp in CHO cells to study the effects of Glut1DS mutations on glucose transport and have used the model to show that Glut1 S65F, R126H, and T295H mutations cause Glut1 deficiency.
Glut1 single-amino acid substitute mutations S65F, R126H, and T295N impair glucose transport activity and membrane association, constituting Glut1-deficient states in vitro.
we have characterized the pathogenic GLUT1 mutations, S66, R126, and T295, and demonstrated that these mutations are pathogenic in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the pathogenicity and functional consequences of the Glut 1 mutations S66F and R126C and the first reported T295M mutation.
the development of an in vitro model to study the pathogenicity and pathophysiology of Glut1DS.
understanding the molecular basis of Glut1DS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Glut1 S, R, and T mutations are Glut1-deficient in vitro and are Glut1DS-causing in vivo.
the S66F, T295M and R126C missense mutations in the GLUT1 gene are associated with Glut1DS.
the pathogenicity in vitro of Glut1 single-amino acid substitute mutations is dependent on the specific amino acid substitution and its location within the Glut1 protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Glut1-Gfp fusion expressed in CHO cell line is applicable for studying Glut1 functional defects and that Glut1 single-amino acid substitute mutations S166F, R126H, and R126C constitute Glut1 deficiency states.
the GLUT1-GFP fusion protein is a useful tool in characterizing the functional consequences of Glut1 missense mutations.
we have shown that the pathogenicity and functional consequences of these three missense mutations can now be studied in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Glut1-GFPI expression model is useful for the characterization of Glut1 single nucleotide mutations and for the identification of Glut1-deficient states in vitro.
Glut1 single missense mutations S66F and T295M are pathogenic and cause Glut1DS.
Glut1-Gfp expression in CHO cells is a useful tool for studying Glut1 function.
